extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing a NIH K01 mentored career development (PA-18-369) application / grant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an NIH K01 (Mentored Research Scientist Development Award) application including SF 424 (R&R), PHS398 career development components, human subjects documentation, budgets, and institutional commitments for a mentored research career-development award.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) Cover Page and Type of Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: SF 424 (R&R) application form fields including Type of Submission (Pre-application / Application / Changed/Corrected Application), Date Submitted, Federal Identifier, Agency Routing Number, Applicant Information (legal name, address), Project Director/PI contact information, Project title, Start and End Dates, Congressional District, and Applicant certifications/assurances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all SF 424(R&R) fields accurately; include authorized representative signature and date; indicate application type (e.g., Resubmission) and whether submitted to other agencies. Follow OMB form requirements (OMB Number, expiration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Always follow funding opportunity's instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction: 'Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FOA-specific requirements (page limits, allowable components, Clinical Trial allowed/not allowed) rather than assuming the sample's format is current; NIAID posts updated samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract (Application component)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise summary describing the goal of the proposed award, research aims, methods, significance, mentorship plan, and candidate effort (e.g., >75% effort to research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain training objectives, research goals, and public health impact; succinctly state aims and planned approaches so reviewers can quickly assess significance and career development potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative (Relevance statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A public-health-oriented narrative describing why the project is important (e.g., how mapping/modeling tools could stretch limited health resources and impact TB/HIV outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a short plain-language statement of the project's relevance to public health for lay readers and non-scientific audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents / Required Application Components
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of all required attachments and subcomponents (Performance Sites; Research & Related Other Project Information; Project Summary/Abstract; Project Narrative; Bibliography & References Cited; Facilities & Other Resources; Equipment; Other Attachments; Research & Related Senior/Key Person; Research & Related Budget Years; Budget Justification; PHS398 Cover Page Supplement; PHS 398 Career Development Award sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble attachments in the FOA-specified order; ensure each listed document is present and named clearly (e.g., FINAL_Abstract_*.pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear enumeration of the research aims that the project will address (used to frame the Research Strategy and evaluation of significance/approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State 2–4 specific, testable aims; align aims with career development and mentorship plans; keep concise and focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed plan of the proposed research methods (geospatial and mathematical modeling in this example) describing aims, rationale, methods, and expected outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient methodological detail for reviewers to assess rigor, feasibility, and potential impact; justify choices and link to preliminary data or literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the candidate's background, career goals, and how the award will support transition to independence (e.g., training in advanced epidemiologic methods, modeling, and implementation science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document candidate's prior experience, planned training activities, percent effort commitment (often >75% for K01), and how the award addresses gaps in skills for future R01 competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement describing plans for training the candidate in responsible conduct (modules, timing, and who will provide training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a specific RCR plan tailored to the candidate (instruction format, frequency, and mentors involved); include documentation that personnel will complete training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-Mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed mentor statements describing their roles, planned interactions, training activities, and support for the candidate's development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include commitments from primary mentor(s) and co-mentors detailing mentoring arrangements, time allocation, and how mentoring will help candidate reach independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters documenting collaborator commitments, roles, and resources they will provide (e.g., data access, analytic support, site collaborations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain signed, role-specific letters that clarify contributions and time commitments; avoid generic letters lacking specifics about the collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Institutional Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement describing the institutional setting and resources available to the candidate (departments, centers, collaborations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the environment provides scientific support, appropriate facilities, and intellectual interactions to foster career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Commitment to Candidate's Research Career Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal institutional statement of commitment (e.g., protected research time, resources, and career development support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a specific institutional commitment letter showing protected effort, funding, and career development resources for the candidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Budget and Budget Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Year-by-year budgets for personnel, consortium F&A, equipment, travel, and other costs, accompanied by narrative justifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare allowable, well-justified budgets aligned with FOA limits; itemize key personnel effort and justify major costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed description of physical, administrative, and collaborative resources available to carry out the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain lab/office space, computing resources, data access, and institutional support; show that necessary infrastructure exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment (Attachment)
rubrics_metrics.description: List and describe equipment to be used for the project (major items and shared instrumentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document access to essential equipment; request new equipment only when justified and allowable per FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete human subjects sections indicating whether human subjects are involved, exempt status, IRB status (pending/approved), and whether the project includes a clinical trial (NIH-defined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate answers (e.g., 'Are Human Subjects Involved? Yes/No'; 'If NO, is IRB review Pending?'), attach Human Subjects documents and IRB approvals when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects (Detailed Plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full description of human subjects protections covering study design, characteristics of subject population, sampling plan, risks, informed consent procedures, data access and management, protections against risk, and rationale for inclusion/exclusion (vulnerable populations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address risks and minimization, informed consent documentation/storage, data confidentiality, recruitment methods, IRB approvals, and specific procedures (e.g., tablet-administered questionnaires; consent forms kept in locked cabinet; coded data on password-protected drives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement whether a data and safety monitoring plan is required (often for clinical trials) and, if required, the proposed monitoring approach (DSMB or other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If study is not a clinical trial and poses minimal risks, explicitly state that a monitoring plan is not required; otherwise, describe monitoring procedures, frequency, and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Enrollment Reports (IER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of planned enrollment locations, populations, and demographic reporting (domestic/foreign enrollment; planned counts by race/ethnicity/sex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide planned recruitment numbers and locations; for foreign studies specify countries and justification, and ensure inclusion reporting follows NIH guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Timeline and Protocol Synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeline of study activities across project years and protocol synopsis including study design, primary purpose, interventions (if any), outcome measures, statistical design and power, subject participation duration, and dissemination plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear Gantt-style timeline for aims and milestones; specify outcomes and analytic approaches (including power calculations where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study-Specific Procedures for Implementation Science (Aim 3 example)
rubrics_metrics.description: For implementation science aims, specify stakeholder engagement procedures, sampling (convenience sampling through mentors' networks), randomization to intervention vs. control presentations, questionnaire administration, and visualization/interface details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe recruitment of stakeholders (numbers, roles), intervention/control conditions (e.g., interactive UI vs. presentation), measures (acceptability, feasibility), and incentives; ensure methods align with human subjects protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Identifiable Private Information and Data Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe collection and storage of identifiers, coding, who has access to linkage files, secure storage (locked cabinets, password-protected online drives), and handling of employment affiliation vs. published comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit access to identifiable data to named personnel, store consent forms securely, keep coded data separate from identifiers, and explain data upload and retention procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Risks, Protections, and Consent Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess minimal risks (e.g., embarrassment), procedures to minimize them (e.g., tablet self-administration), documentation of written informed consent, and protections (training of research staff, locked storage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain risk mitigation measures, training requirements for staff (e.g., RCR training), and absence/presence of anticipated medical interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for Inclusion or Exclusion of Vulnerable Populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement explaining whether vulnerable populations (as defined by HHS) are included and rationale if excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If excluding vulnerable populations, justify; if including, describe additional protections and consent/assent procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Benefits and Importance of Knowledge Gained
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain expected direct benefits to participants (if any) and broader benefits to public health, policy, or scientific knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify that participants may not directly benefit but describe how findings could improve decision-making or resource allocation and state the importance of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Items: Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, Consortium/Contractual Agreements, Resource Sharing, Authentication of Key Biological/Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate protocol attachments/sections indicating applicability and details for vertebrate animals; select agent usage; consortium or contractual arrangements; resource sharing plans; and authentication of key reagents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each domain, state 'Not applicable' if not relevant or provide required documentation (IACUC approvals, MTAs, data-sharing plans, authentication methods) per NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Justification and International Collaboration Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: When research involves activities outside the U.S., provide countries involved and an explanation/justification (e.g., research in Uganda), plus foreign justification attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why foreign sites are necessary, describe collaborating institutions (e.g., Makerere University), and include agreements and local approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Assignment to Groups and Randomization
rubrics_metrics.description: If the design includes assignment/randomization, describe assignment procedures (e.g., randomizing stakeholders to interactive forum vs. presentation) and clarify that some parts may have no assigned groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail allocation methods, masking (if any), and how intervention/control conditions differ; ensure this aligns with IRB-approved protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for dissemination of study results (publications, presentations, policy briefings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how findings will be communicated to stakeholders, policy-makers, and the scientific community; include timelines if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with FOIA and Confidentiality/Redaction Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIAID note on FOIA: FOIA requests may lead to redactions protecting confidential commercial/financial info, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that publicly posted sample applications and summary statements may have redactions and that applicants should not expect all internal review content to be public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Designation and Related Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Indication whether the FOA/application allows clinical trials (e.g., 'Clinical Trial: Not Allowed') and whether a study is an NIH-defined Phase III clinical trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FOA clinical trial policy: if trials are not allowed, do not propose interventional clinical trials; if included, meet clinical trial requirements (registration, monitoring, informed consent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent Effort / Protected Research Time for Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of the candidate's proposed percent effort (example: 'This award will support Dr. Ross to dedicate more than 75% of her effort to research').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For K awards, document protected effort consistent with FOA (often majority/proportion specified); ensure budgets and institutional commitment letters reflect this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship/Use of Sample Application Material and Attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Permission note: awardee provided permission for NIAID to post this grant application for educational purposes; use is allowed for nonprofit educational purposes only if material remains unchanged and original investigators and NIH NIAID are credited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect copyright and attribution statements when using sample materials.
